$comment: SUB-013 — real `parameters` objects checked against the derived encodings at generation time.
Criterion 3 says a reader following SCHEMA.md alone can author a valid States node, including
`value-true-bg color`. That is a claim about a document, and the only way to stop it rotting is
to check the document's own worked example mechanically, every time the catalog is built.
Two checks run over each entry. `shape` asks whether every key matches a derived pattern or a
static port — can this key exist on this node at all. `references` asks whether the names
interpolated into it are actually present in the parameters they are drawn from — does this key
reach anything. A key can pass the first and fail the second, and that combination is precisely
the failure the task exists to expose: it reaches the runtime, matches no generated port, and
`expectedOrphans` are keys known to fail the second check. They are listed, not tolerated in
bulk: an unlisted orphan fails generation, and a listed one that stops being an orphan does too.

examples.orphanNote: Carried over verbatim from the shipped prefab the spec quotes, and orphaned there too — there is no state called `on`. Kept because it is what a real file looks like, and because the example is more honest for showing that the format does not stop you writing one.

examples.name: toggle-switch prefab, as shipped
examples.why: The file SUB-013 opens with. Every key is shape-valid, and six of them reach nothing — which is the case neither the editor nor SUB-006 catches today.
examples.orphanNote: `values` is `pos` alone and `states` is `true,false`, so every key naming `bg color`, `border color`, `on` or `off` is a leftover from an earlier edit. The node renders correctly — the runtime generates no port for them, so they are simply never read. Nothing in the editor, the runtime or the validator says a word about it.
